posts.body_html: After another flush with a few gallons of rainwater, the peat that started at about 80 and measured 45/63 yesterday is now down to 11/13 ppm. I have removed it from the drained bin and placed it in an undrained tub. I want to let it sit in water for a day or two without any leaching to see if the salt levels start to rise again. If they don't, it might be ready to use for the seedlings under lights!

posts.body_html: We had 3-6" of rain overnight (!) and the peat bins read a glorious 6 ppm this morning, ambient temp. I took some and stuck it in a gallon ziploc bag and I'm going to measure the fluids over time to see if more salts come out, as was Mike's experience. Overall though I am pleasantly surprised at how fast the salt levels dropped. My next project is going to be to try to flush the nasty-ass Sunshine peat I bought at home cheapo last week. It read 175 in cold water, so it would def be above 200 in grow temps. Wish me luck!

posts.body_html:
Dec 8, 2015 1:26:12 GMT -5 hunter said:
calen,i am interested in what you find out,i measured my ppm in my bogs and it was 160 ppm and i think thats what is causing some of my problems,i then checked my seedlings which are separate and doing well and only measured 75 ppm which is about the same as my tap water,do you think its better to soak the peat or just rinse?
What's up Hunter! Yeah 160 is pushing it for sure! A few years back I used 140 ppm tap water for my water tables and things did okaaaay but the red flavas weren't red and I had some losses from rot. Not sure exactly what you mean by soaking vs rinsing? What you want to do is saturate the peat, let the water pick up the salts in the peat, then get the water out of there taking the salt with it. So just soaking won't help at all if the water and salts just stay in bog. Your bogs are raised planters IIRC so if there are drain holes anywhere you should be able to just run a bunch of water through them - flood and drain, flood and drain, flood and drain. If the drain water tests higher than in the input water then you are removing salts. The purer the water you flush with, the more salt you can remove per unit of water, and the lower you can get the salt levels overall. I've been lucky to have a bunch of 0 ppm rainwater to flush with and it's been super fast, but flushing with your 75 ppm tap water I'd think you could get the bog ppm down to about 75 fairly quickly as well. Good luck and keep us posted!

Update: it's been a little slower with this stuff, but after several days of rain and pouring water through, the formerly radioactive Sunshine is down to 75 ppm at room temperature. posts.body_html:
quick update on the sphagnum trays. To recap, I harvested a wheel barrel full of moss a few months ago, chopped up some tops, and placed them in 10x20 trays. Hopefully in one year, they'll produce another wheel barrel full of moss.

We had some temps. around 29F (~-2C) for a few days in December or January, and some of the moss that was "taller" froze. Patches of my new moss beds were brown days afterwards and it took a very long time to recover from the freezing. Here's some new photos, taken 2/19/16:


this "chunk" turned brown and at one point, it looked like the whole tray was going to die, but it's clearly making a great comeback:


You can still see patches of brown where the moss was damaged, but overall, they're making a great comeback now that we have mild, sunny days:


One last shot:


Maybe harvesting Sphagnum in the fall isn't the best idea...perhaps spring is better? No idea....

posts.body_html:
Indeed, just about everywhere sphagnum grows in the US, it freezes regularly. I think being in a pot makes them more susceptible to freeze injury much like Sarracenias. Also, getting them to grow and establish in the fall, and then all of the sudden freeze probably creates more damage compared to an established bed that naturally slows down in growth and then freezes over.

Eric-it would be pretty darn amazing to have a fat sphagnum bog, plus you'll be able to harvest it every year for whatever cropz you got going. Maybe jump in there and make angel wings before harvesting
